sentence: a sanitized NCCL receipt on three cards at Gen2 x16 behind PLX switches measures 6.63–6.68 GB/s host-staged copy [[readmemd]] (T2)

The note's host-staged copy measurement is cuMemcpyPeer at 256 MiB = 6.21–6.30 GB/s; 6.68 GB/s is the note's single-card D2H reference (a different configuration, not a host-staged inter-card copy), and 6.63 GB/s appears nowhere in this note — it is the ocl_pcie_bw figure from physical-modsmd / pcie-subsystemmd on a different rig. The report's own Source Tensions section already uses the correct 6.21–6.30 GB/s figure for this rig, so §1 is internally inconsistent.

sentence: At Gen2 x16, NCCL reaches 3.69–4.24 GB/s busbw against a 6.63–6.68 GB/s one-way rate — 53–64% of the link [[readmemd]] (T2/T4)
problem: The busbw half is supported (3.69 / 3.85 / 4.24 GB/s). The one-way-rate half is not: the note's one-way figures are 6.68 GB/s (single-card D2H reference) and 6.21–6.30 GB/s (cuMemcpyPeer host-staged copy); 6.63 GB/s is absent. The derived efficiency band is also off at the low end — 3.69/6.68 = 55.2%, so the band is 55–64%, not 53–64%.
evidence: readmemd: busbw 3.69 GB/s (same-switch pair), 3.85 GB/s (cross-switch pair), 4.24 GB/s (all three); cuMemcpyPeer 6.21–6.30 GB/s; D2H reference 6.68 GB/s.
suggested_fix: Use 6.68 GB/s (single-card D2H reference) as the one-way rate and 55–64% as the efficiency band; or use 6.21–6.30 GB/s and 59–68%. Drop the 6.63 lower bound, which is not in this note.

sentence: TileLang's own fallback to it "runs 1.81× slower", so an sm_80 build is possible-but-slow rather than impossible

The note never mentions sm_80, Ampere, or an sm_80 build, so the inference 'an sm_80 build is possible-but-slow rather than impossible' is the report's own extrapolation.
suggested_fix: Soften to what the note supports: 'TileLang's own `mma.sync` fallback path runs 1.81× slower on H800 SXM, so an sm_80 build would be slower still — the note contains no sm_80 measurement.'
